16K views · 85 reactions | The Hoover Dam's Concrete Is Still Curing - 90 Years Later 

The concrete inside the Hoover Dam is technically still curing, nearly 90 years after construction finished in 1936, because concrete this massive simply never fully stops its chemical hardening process. Engineers at the time faced a real problem: pouring the dam's full volume in one continuous mass would have generated so much internal heat from curing that it might have taken over a century to cool and set properly, risking cracks. Their solution was to embed nearly 600 miles of steel cooling pipes directly into the concrete, circulating cold river water to manage the heat as it set in sections. That improvised cooling system became a standard technique used in large concrete structures worldwide ever since. Sometimes solving one massive engineering problem quietly changes an entire industry's practices for decades after.
